title: Sandia and Quantinuum Introduce Logical Gate Set Tomography to Map Fault-Tolerant Qubit Noise - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Sandia National Laboratories and Quantinuum introduced Logical Gate Set Tomography and used it on the 20-qubit H1-1 to fully reconstruct a universal single-qubit logical gate set encoded in the [[7,1,3]] Steane code. The 50-shot hardware data fit the Pauli-stochastic noise assumed by threshold theorems. High-shot emulation, however, exposed small logical non-Markovianity and coherent over-rotations, which the researchers traced mainly to dephasing during ion transport and cooling.

insights.claim: Logical GST gives the first self-consistent, full tomographic reconstruction of a universal single-qubit logical gate set. It extends physical-layer characterization to encoded, fault-tolerant operations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Logical qubits can now be audited with the same rigor as physical gates, which matters for checking fault-tolerance claims.

insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Logical benchmarks that rely on Pauli-frame tracking may understate coherent errors.

insights.claim: The characterized gate set included transversal Clifford gates and a non-transversal T gate made via magic-state injection and teleportation, with a 95.9% acceptance rate per attempt. Measured logical entanglement infidelities included 0.7% for H, 0.2% for S and 1.2% for T, though the error bars were wide.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Universal logical gate sets now sit around the 1% error level on trapped ions.

themes.theme: Validating the noise models behind fault tolerance

insights.claim: The 50-shot H1-1 data, across 158 compressed circuits, fit a Pauli-stochastic model with no statistically significant non-Markovian memory effects. This supports the assumption in threshold theorems that QEC turns physical noise into simple uncorrelated channels.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is early experimental support for the noise models that fault-tolerance roadmaps rely on, though limited by low shot counts.

insights.claim: 14,100-shot simulations on Quantinuum's H1-1E emulator revealed small but statistically significant logical non-Markovianity and coherent logical over-rotations of about 0.0015π. Toggling error channels showed that physical dephasing during ion transport and sympathetic cooling is the main cause of the coherent drift.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Ion shuttling and cooling are key engineering targets for keeping logical errors well-behaved as trapped-ion systems scale.

insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This could become a standard verification tool for fault-tolerance claims across hardware vendors.
